subject: humanities
passage: Some teachers argue that listening to an audiobook is not really reading. In their view, students who listen to a story instead of looking at the printed words will understand and remember less of it.
passage_b: Psychologist Tomás Ferreira tested this idea with a group of adult volunteers. Half of them read a short history book in print, and half listened to a recording of the same book. On a test given afterward, the two groups answered about the same number of questions correctly. Ferreira concluded that, at least for this kind of book, listening and reading led to similar understanding.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the view of the teachers in Text 1?

choices.A: By agreeing that people who listen to books remember less than readers do
choices.B: By arguing that audiobooks are better than print for every type of book
choices.C: By suggesting that schools should replace printed books with recordings
choices.D: By noting that in one test, listeners understood a book as well as readers

explanation.why: The teachers in Text 1 claim that listeners "will understand and remember less." In Text 2, Ferreira's listeners and readers "answered about the same number of questions correctly," so he concluded that listening and reading led to "similar understanding." The author of Text 2 would answer the teachers by pointing to this result.
explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the teachers' view in Text 1; Text 2's test found that the two groups did about equally well.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Text 2 found similar results, not better ones, and limits its conclusion to "this kind of book."
explanation.C: Incorrect. Text 2 does not recommend replacing printed books; it only compares understanding.
explanation.D: Correct. Text 2 reports that listeners and readers did about equally well on the test, which challenges the teachers' claim.
